req.title: Status code sentence body
req.statement: The system shall include the standard reason phrase in the body when responding to /status/<code> with a code between 400 and 599.

doc.reasoning: R-HTTPBIN-045 requires that GET /status/<code> for codes 400-599 returns a response whose body contains the standard HTTP reason phrase. The status_code() helper in helpers.py builds the response via make_response() and sets r.status_code; for most codes in 400-599 it does NOT override r.data, so Flask/Werkzeug populates the status line but the body may be empty or contain the phrase depending on implementation. We must test: (1) a representative 4xx code body contains the reason phrase (positive/EP), (2) a representative 5xx code body contains the reason phrase (positive/EP), (3) the boundary at exactly 400 (BVA lower bound), (4) the boundary at exactly 599 (BVA upper bound), (5) code 399 is outside the range (BVA boundary-1), (6) code 600 is outside the range (BVA boundary+1), (7) a code with a special override like 402 still returns 2xx HTTP transport and correct body (DT), (8) a non-numeric code returns 400 (NEG). Tests assert exact status codes and exact body content to kill constant-mutation and comparison-mutation operators.

tests.name: test_status_400_body_contains_reason_phrase
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
GET /status/400 is a valid endpoint
expected: HTTP response status code is exactly 400
Response body contains 'BAD REQUEST' (case-insensitive)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-045: 400-599 responses must include standard reason phrase in body
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_status_400_body_contains_reason_phrase():
    r = client.get('/status/400')
    assert r.status_code == 400
    body = r.data.decode('utf-8', errors='replace').upper()
    assert 'BAD REQUEST' in body

tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_status_401_body_not_empty():
    r = client.get('/status/401')
    assert r.status_code == 401
    www_auth = r.headers.get('WWW-Authenticate', '')
    assert 'Basic' in www_auth
    assert 'Fake Realm' in www_auth
